A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LDMol by the same authors. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, including material renamed or moved between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original LDMol generation, retrieval and ablation measurements in Tables 1–3, together with generation, editing and appendix retrieval examples.

after.justification: v2 reports original LDMol measurements and adds encoder-feature analysis, quantitative editing comparisons and guidance-scale experiments, including appendix results.

M1.justification: The contrastive SMILES encoder, stereoisomer negatives, compression layer, autoregressive decoder, conditional DiT, retrieval scoring and DDS editing procedure are retained. Specifying MolT5large and adding architecture diagrams and pseudocode clarify implementation rather than establish a changed method. The new editing benchmark uses a null source prompt within the existing DDS procedure.

E1.justification: v2 substantially extends editing coverage from structural examples to eight property-directed scenarios involving solubility, drug-likeness, permeability and hydrogen bonding on ZINC15 molecules. ZINC15 also replaces PubChem as the source of unlabeled diffusion-training molecules. The principal paired datasets remain; the MoMu retrieval test set is the earlier Su et al. custom set under another name.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds T5large, MolT5large, MolXPT, bioT5 and bioT5+, and removes SciBERT from that comparison. Table 2 adds MoleculeSTM and MolCA. Figure 5 adds an editing comparison against MoleculeSTM(Graph), while Figure 3 and Table 3 introduce a KL-regularized autoencoder comparator. These substantially strengthen and broaden the comparison methods.

E3.justification: Reported settings change substantially: unlabeled training samples decrease from 100,000 to 10,000, DiT batch size increases from 16 to 64 per GPU, and ChEBI-20 guidance changes from 3.5 to 2.5. Editing examples change from 200 iterations, learning rate 0.4 and guidance 2.0 to 150, 0.1 and 2.5. New protocols include 200-molecule editing evaluations, normalized feature distances for 1,000 random and 1,000 enumerated pairs, and additional ablation metrics. Guidance selection now explicitly uses the reported test-set sweep.

E4.justification: v2 adds an encoder-invariance diagnostic comparing enumerated and random SMILES pairs (Figure 3), ablations of stereoisomer negatives and KL regularization (Table 3), and a classifier-free guidance sensitivity study (Appendix B.1). The original contrastive-pretraining and compression ablations remain. Appendix retrieval cases expand from two to four, and generation/editing examples are revised.

E5.justification: Figure 5(a) newly reports means and variability error bars over three separate editing runs, described as 'standard variation' in its caption. v1 has no corresponding run-based uncertainty reporting. The retrieval averaging over n=10 or n=25 noise evaluations is retained.

E6.justification: LDMol results are revised throughout Tables 1–3. Table 1 exact match changes from 0.363 to 0.530 and FCD from 0.25 to 0.20. At n=25, Table 2 PCdes paragraph accuracy changes from 90.82% to 90.3%, and MoMu paragraph accuracy from 81.13% to 87.1%. Changed training and sampling settings prevent interpreting these as controlled same-setting gains. New results include KL-regularized generation with 0.492 exact match, stereoisomer ablations, guidance curves and editing hit ratios favoring LDMol in five of eight scenarios.

T1.justification: The diffusion equations and contrastive/reconstruction objectives remain substantively equivalent. v2 makes the decoder's latent conditioning explicit and expresses the existing guidance and downstream procedures in pseudocode. Its added invariance and mutual-information discussion is conceptual motivation, without new formal assumptions, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The main molecular-generation, contrastive-representation and downstream-task contributions remain. v2 adds the broader claim that LDMol is among the first diffusion models to surpass autoregressive models in text generation and suggests implications for natural-language diffusion. The zero-shot generation claim disappears from the abstract but remains in Section 4.1.

C2.justification: v2 develops a substantive explanation connecting SMILES enumeration, structural invariance and mutual information, and interprets the new KL, stereoisomer and guidance analyses. It newly prioritizes ground-truth agreement over validity when stronger baselines have higher validity. The conclusion removes v1's editing-hyperparameter-sensitivity limitation while retaining the difficulty with biological-property prompts.

D1.justification: v2 specifies MolT5large, expands DiT embedding and conditioning details in Appendix A.1, and documents null-source editing and scenario hyperparameter ranges in Appendix A.3. However, Table 4 removes GPU hardware and training-time information, and the ChEBI-specific fine-tuning description disappears. This establishes lost documentation, not that fine-tuning was actually discontinued.

R1.justification: Beyond v1's emphasis on TGM-DLM, v2 positions LDMol against geometric latent diffusion by Xu et al. and language latent diffusion by Lovelace et al. It develops its relationship to SMILES enumeration and contrastive augmentation through additional cited work, and adds references supporting new comparators. This substantially expands research positioning beyond the switch to author-year citations.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory motivation, encoder rationale and experimental narrative receive substantial rewriting. Appendices A–C are reorganized into Experimental Details and Additional Results with new subsections. The title, terminology, author presentation and citation style also change.

P2.justification: v2 redraws overview and example figures, adds encoder-distance, DiT-block and guidance figures, and combines editing examples with a new error-bar chart. Table 1 gains a model-family column, and Table 3 gains grouped reconstruction/generation columns. The downstream pipeline is retained as Figure 7, while retrieval examples are redesigned and expanded as Figure 9. The document template and layout also change throughout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for the central representation-learning claim through the regularized-latent comparison, encoder-invariance diagnostic and stereoisomer ablation missing from v1. Stronger baselines and quantitative editing results with repeated-run variability also address important weaknesses in the earlier evaluation. These gains outweigh the lost hardware/fine-tuning documentation and removed editing-sensitivity caveat, although selecting guidance using ChEBI-20 test results weakens benchmark independence.
